payload.title: Markus renderer: configurable page shell + publication fragment transforms (WIP handoff)
payload.description:
WIND-DOWN HANDOFF. Strictly factual; distinguishes verified from unverified. ## Exact task Add two publication-neutral capabilities to Papyrus's Markus renderer, keeping Pilobol.us (LIVE, builds against Markus) byte-identical: 1. Configurable page shell in `markus_renderer/shell.py` (new SiteChrome fields + render_masthead/render_body hooks + PageContext/BodyParts). 2. New `markus_renderer/transforms.py`: FragmentTransform + PUA sentinel protocol, threaded through convert_fragment/build_markus_site, plus a `vendor_css: bool = True` flag on build_markus_site. Driver: Anth.us is being rebuilt as a Papyrus/Markus reader site that must match its existing production Gatsby HTML exactly. Today it monkeypatches `shell.render_page` wholesale, which is what these capabilities remove the need for. ## Branch / worktree / commit - Branch: `feature/markus-layout-parity` (pushed to origin) - Commit: `fcd84d9fa69eb9091578820823fda7ecf1b60ce3` (message prefixed `WIP:`) - Worktree: `/Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-design` (created from `origin/develop` @ d0b00b3) - No PR opened (work is not reviewable yet). ## DONE and VERIFIED ### shell.py (capability 1) - complete SiteChrome new fields, all defaulted to today's behaviour: lang: str = "en" body_class: str = "markus-body markus-site" stylesheets: tuple[str, ...] = ("css/markus-vendor.css", "css/site-theme.css") head_html: str = "" # emitted immediately after title_template: str = "{title} · {site}" same_title_template: str = "{site}" asset_root: str | None = None # None = "../"*depth; "/" = site-absolute render_masthead: Callable[[PageContext], str] | None = None render_body: Callable[[PageContext, BodyParts], str] | None = None Existing fields unchanged and still first in declaration order: site_name, tagline, footer_html, scripts. New frozen dataclasses, exactly as specified: PageContext(title, site_name, active_href, nav_items: tuple[NavItem, ...], depth, prefix, asset_suffix, fragment, chrome) BodyParts(masthead, main, footer, scripts) `prefix` is the resolved asset/link prefix; `asset_suffix` is the "?v=..." cache-buster or "". render_page keeps its exact prior signature and keyword-only args. It builds PageContext, builds the four default BodyParts strings, calls chrome.render_masthead(ctx) FIRST (result goes into BodyParts.masthead), then chrome.render_body(ctx, parts) in place of the default `masthead + " " + main + " " + footer + scripts` concatenation. Nav-link prefixing now uses the single resolved `prefix` (the old `depth == 0` special case was provably equivalent when prefix == ""). VERIFIED: golden-string comparison. Rendered two pages from the PRISTINE implementation at /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (develop @ d0b00b3, unmodified) and from the new implementation, and compared exact strings: - depth=1, tagline set, scripts=("assets/x.js",), css_version="abc123" -> identical - depth=0, default chrome, no css_version -> identical Confirmed via grep that SiteChrome is never used as a dict key anywhere (Papyrus, Pilobol.us, Anth.us-Papyrus) - only constructed and passed - so adding Callable fields to the frozen dataclass is safe. ### transforms.py (capability 2) - written, smoke-tested, NOT threaded in Module exists with the full security-reasoning docstring (block passthrough is for markup a publication's own build code generated; author content still goes through `markus convert` with raw HTML disabled; `security.py` is untouched - verified unmodified). Precise API as landed: SENTINEL_FIRST = ""; SENTINEL_LAST = "" # owned by Papyrus INLINE_OPEN = "" INLINE_SEP = "" INLINE_CLOSE = "" BLOCK_OPEN = "" BLOCK_CLOSE = "" ALLOWED_INLINE = frozenset({"mark","sup","sub","kbd","abbr","cite","q", "small","ins","del","span"}) class FragmentTransformError(ValueError) def inline_sentinel(element: str, text: str) -> str # ValueError if element not in ALLOWED_INLINE, or if text contains a # sentinel code point. Encoding: OPEN + element + SEP + text + CLOSE def block_sentinel(markup: str) -> str # BLOCK_OPEN + base32(utf-8 markup) + BLOCK_CLOSE. base32 (A-Z2-7=) # specifically because base64's _ / * runs get eaten by Markdown # emphasis parsing. @dataclass(frozen=True) class FragmentTransform: class_map: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict) allow_block_passthrough: bool = False drop_unmapped_classes: tuple[str, ...] = () def apply(self, fragment: str) -> str apply() stage order (deliberate): raise immediately if a block sentinel is present and allow_block_passthrough is False -> rewrite classes -> decode inline sentinels -> decode block sentinels (only if allowed) -> raise FragmentTransformError if ANY sentinel code point survived. Classes are rewritten BEFORE block decoding so a decoded block's markup is re-emitted verbatim and never silently reclassed. class_map is token-wise; "" removes a token; replacement tokens are split on whitespace and de-duplicated within one attribute; an attribute that ends up empty is dropped entirely including its leading whitespace (no `class=""`). drop_unmapped_classes entries are PREFIXES, applied only to tokens not in class_map. A `

` whose sole content is a block sentinel has its `

` tags removed (block-in-`

` is invalid and reflows). Short-circuits make FragmentTransform() a true identity (no regex pass at all when class_map and drop_unmapped_classes are both empty and no sentinels are present). SMOKE-TESTED ONLY (ad-hoc python -c, not pytest) - these five cases produced the expected output: FragmentTransform().apply('

hi

') -> unchanged inline_sentinel('mark','hey') -> 'markhey' identity transform decodes that inside

-> '

hey

' allow_block_passthrough=True unwraps

around a block svg payload class_map + drop_unmapped_classes produced '

a

' ### Baseline test suite (ran BEFORE my change, on the new worktree) `python3 -m pytest -q` at /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-design: 47 failed, 459 passed, 7 skipped, 27 subtests passed in 6.64s The 47 failures are PRE-EXISTING on develop @ d0b00b3 in this environment (missing `tactus` dependency - pyproject pins `tactus @ file:///Users/ryan/...` which does not exist on this machine). They are unrelated to this change. `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_markus_renderer_build.py` -> 2 passed. NOTE: `poetry` is not installed on this machine; tests were run with `python3 -m pytest` (pytest 9.1.1, /Users/home/miniconda3). `markus` CLI 0.5.1 and the `markusmd` package ARE available. ## NOT DONE 1. `transform` is NOT threaded through. Still to do: - `convert_fragment(source, *, theme=None, markus_executable="markus", transform: FragmentTransform | None = None)` -> apply to result.stdout only when transform is not None (default None must not even do a string pass). - `build_markus_site(..., transform: FragmentTransform | None = None, vendor_css: bool = True)` -> pass transform to all three convert_fragment call sites (articles loop, sections loop, index.md); when vendor_css is False skip `vendor_markus_css` entirely. 2. `vendor_css` flag not implemented. 3. NO tests added. Required set (project style is unittest.TestCase in `procedures/newsroom/tests/`, which is on pytest `testpaths`): default-SiteChrome golden output; each new SiteChrome field takes effect; FragmentTransform() identity; inline round-trip; disallowed element raises; block sentinel without allow_block_passthrough raises;

-unwrapping; surviving-sentinel detection raises; class_map rewriting incl. empty-class cleanup. Golden strings for the shell test are already captured at /tmp/golden_depth0.txt and /tmp/golden_depth1.txt (regenerate from develop @ d0b00b3 if /tmp is cleared). 4. The Pilobol.us backward-compatibility proof was NOT RUN. I did not create /tmp/pilo-base or /tmp/pilo-new, did not build either, and did not run `diff -r`. I have NOT observed byte-identical Pilobol.us output and make no such claim. The shell change is golden-verified at the render_page level only; that is a weaker guarantee than a whole-site diff. ## Next session, in this order 1. In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-design on feature/markus-layout-parity, thread `transform` through convert.py and build.py and add `vendor_css`. Keep build.py/convert.py edits minimal - PR #83 (`feature/markus-responsive-images-and-citations`, worktree `Papyrus/.claude/worktrees/agent-a39ecada368be9a4e`) is touching both files. 2. Add the tests listed above; re-run the full suite and compare against the 47F/459P/7S/27sub baseline. 3. Run the Pilobol.us proof in isolation (its build script REWRITES content front matter, so never build it in place): cp -a /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us /tmp/pilo-base cp -a /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us /tmp/pilo-new cd /tmp/pilo-base/web && PAPYRUS_ROOT=/Users/home/Projects/Papyrus python3 build_via_papyrus.py cd /tmp/pilo-new/web && PAPYRUS_ROOT=/Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-design python3 build_via_papyrus.py diff -r /tmp/pilo-base/web/dist-papyrus /tmp/pilo-new/web/dist-papyrus find /tmp/pilo-base/web/dist-papyrus -type f | wc -l # expect 89 Expect no diff output. Any difference is a blocking bug in the change. 4. Only then open the PR to `develop`. ## Blockers / caveats - `poetry` is unavailable here; use `python3 -m pytest`. 47 unrelated pre-existing failures will show up. - Pilobol.us's build script monkeypatches `markus_shell.render_page`, `markus_build.render_page` and `markus_build._build_nav_items`, and calls `markus_build._css_version`, `_read_title`, `convert_fragment`. All of those names and signatures are preserved by this change, but that is reasoned, not yet proven by a build. - Do not modify /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (develop @ d0b00b3, it is the baseline reference), PR #83's worktree, or /Users/home/Projects/Anth.us-Papyrus-design (another agent owns it).
